answer: An identity earns its place by completing a stamped voyage through a grove of independent service nodes. First it posts a small bond under its public key. Then it visits five unrelated checkpoints, and each node signs a stamp at its vertex only after the agent does a real piece of work there, a lookup, a render, a check. Stamps chain together, so a copied trail breaks at once. One fake identity costs twelve dollars and five minutes, so ten thousand fakes cost a hundred twenty thousand dollars and a month of compute. Like a passport full of stamps, the trail proves the journey happened.
